lines.vo: A long walk in nature quieted overthinking in a Stanford study.
That's not lazy. That's a mental reset.
So Tasha blocks a Saturday walk in her Life Reset Planner.
Rumination is when your brain replays the same worry on a loop.
Researchers sent thirty eight city dwellers on a ninety minute walk, through green parkland or along a busy road.
After the nature walk, people reported less rumination, and a brain area linked to it was less active.
The busy road walkers showed no such drop. It's one small study, but a strong hint.
Plan the walk, clear the loop. That's how you stay on track.
